words: I'll take the tidal margins. If those figures are to settle what the crew believes is possible, they must be exact — I'll work through every calculation carefully.
Understood. Modeling the tidal margins calls for steady, honest numbers, and that is what I'll give. I'll begin the work you've offered me.
I accept the agreement you offered, Captain. I'll prepare the medical bay with care — for an approach no one aboard has come through with their memories intact, it must be ready.
You'll have my agreement for the medic work. I'm frightened of what this approach does to memories, but the bay must be prepared — I'll see to it myself.
So the plan is I step back and rest before whatever comes next. I don't need it. Count me out of this one.
Log the rest offer as declined. I'm tense, not tired, and I don't step aside just because someone says it's time.

Captain, I hear your call to hold the vigil in the Cathedral, and it troubles me: we keep watch for crew who will not remember this approach afterwards. I fear the vigil must carry all their remembering for them.

My concern is not the rite, Captain, but who it serves: crew who will not remember this approach afterwards. I worry the vigil in the Cathedral may be a devotion they will never know was kept for them.
About the agreement to brace the bubble generator — I can't sign off on it yet. Those mounts carry parts the ship can't replace, and I'm not committing half-ready.
Not yet, Captain. Bracing the bubble generator against tidal stress with parts we can't replace — I'm not putting my name on that agreement until my head is clear.
Fine, I'll accept the agreement. No use pretending the strain isn't catching up with me. I'll step back and rest before taking on the next assignment.
Rest, then. I'd rather stay on task, but I can't honestly argue with the state I'm in. I'll take the break you're offering.
I accept, Captain. I will keep the vigil in the Cathedral for the crew who will not remember this approach — the hours will not be left empty.
Then I will stand the vigil as you ask, Captain. Faith holds where memory fails, and I will hold it for them in the Cathedral.
Understood, Captain. I'll brace the generator mounts against the tidal stress — carefully, since we can't replace those parts.
Agreed. I'll get the bubble generator's mounts braced for the tidal stress — with parts we can't replace, I'll do it right, not fast.
The start is agreed, Captain. I'll keep at the tidal margins, working the figures methodically — and I'll say plainly where the numbers waver.
You've marked the start agreed; I'm back on the tidal margins. These numbers settle how close the ship can pass before tides turn fatal — I'll keep them exact.
Captain, I've started on the medical bay as we agreed, but the strain is getting to me. Could someone spell me for a while? I want a clear head for work this delicate.
You asked me to ready the medical bay and I gave my word to begin — I have. But I need a breather. Would you send someone to take my place for a bit, Captain?
